cars.variant: SHO 3.0 V6 manual — 1989 USA introduction reference
cars.specification_market: 1989 USA Taurus SHO, original Ford introduction brochure reference. Retain its advertised 220 hp and 200 lb-ft without assuming an unstated gross/net standard or converting units. The brochure specifies a 3.0-litre V6, Yamaha collaboration, DOHC/four valves per cylinder, sequential multipoint injection, dual-runner intake and EEC-IV control. Its 7000-rpm redline is not a claim about fuel-cut speed; an embedded magazine quotation is not technical authority. The contemporary independent test supplies five-speed manual and front-wheel drive only. Exact cc, output-peak rpm, acceleration, maximum speed and later 3.2-litre automatic/3.4 V8/EcoBoost AWD values are not imported. Count the original 1989–1995 Yamaha-V6 sporting-road lineage once across related body revisions, transmissions, trim and years.
cars.summary: The original Taurus SHO made Yamaha’s four-cam, 24-valve V6 the centrepiece of a discreet American performance saloon. A manual drivetrain and revised independent chassis supported the engine, and its contemporary road test established the SHO as a landmark in accessible sports-saloon performance.

cars.variant: Standard SRT-4 — 2005 USA factory downloadable-brochure reference
cars.specification_market: Standard 2005 USA Dodge SRT-4, original five-page Dodge/DaimlerChrysler downloadable brochure reference. The cover explicitly says 2005; PDF pages 1 and 4 supply the selected specification. Retain advertised 230 hp at 5300 rpm and 250 lb-ft at 2200–4400 rpm without inferring a gross/net convention, kW conversion or dyno output. Standard New Venture T-850 five-speed manual, front drive, Quaife ATB limited-slip, 17 × 6 wheels and 205/50R17 tyres are explicit. The 5.8-second 0–60-mph field is a manufacturer claim, not the 2004 test car’s measured time. No maximum-speed figure is imported because the brochure’s claim and independent earlier-car test differ. Count the original Neon SRT-4 road family once across 2003–2005 tunes, ACR/Commemorative packages, equipment and names; no ordinary Neon, staged Mopar tune or Caliber SRT4 is added.
cars.summary: The Neon-based SRT-4 became a defining American factory sport compact. Its turbocharged engine, manual gearbox and torque-biasing differential delivered an accessible performance formula supported by contemporary instrumented evaluation and comparison-test success.
